name: Row
pattern: Horizontal pull: the hands pull a load toward the torso while the shoulder blades squeeze back, the trunk held still.
setup: Bar over the middle of your feet, feet hip width, knees soft.
Hinge at the hips until your chest leans well forward, back flat, neck long.
Let your arms hang straight under your shoulders, grip just wider than shoulder width.

steps.text: Start with arms long and shoulder blades slightly spread, back flat.
Squeeze your shoulder blades back first, then drive your elbows back toward your hips.
Touch the bar to your lower ribs or belly, chest still, and hold for a moment.
Straighten your arms under control and let the shoulder blades glide forward again.

cues.cue: Flat back, hips hinged, trunk does not move.
cues.why: The bent-over row gives the highest lower-back load of common rows; a still, braced trunk keeps that load safe.

cues.cue: Start each pull by squeezing your shoulder blades together.
cues.why: Rowing is one of the core exercises for the mid trapezius and rhomboids, which pull the shoulder blades back.

cues.cue: Drive your elbows back toward your hips, not your hands up.
cues.why: Thinking about the back, not the arms, raises lat activity and lowers rear-delt takeover.

cues.cue: Shoulders down, away from your ears.
cues.why: Shrugging shifts work to the upper trapezius instead of the mid and lower trapezius.

cues.cue: Arms fully long at the bottom, bar to your belly at the top.
cues.why: Letting the shoulder blades move through their range trains both the pull and the reach; fixing them only changes where the muscles work.

breathing: Breathe in and brace before you pull, breathe out as you lower or at the top.

tempo.note: Pull in about 1 second, hold the squeeze, lower in 2.

mistakes.name: Back rounds
mistakes.looks: The lower back curves and the chest drops toward the floor as you pull.
mistakes.fix: Brace, push your hips back and keep your chest proud; use less weight.
mistakes.why: A flexed lower spine under a hanging load raises spine compression; the bent-over row already has the highest load of the rows tested.

mistakes.name: Body heaves
mistakes.looks: The trunk swings up with each rep to throw the bar back.
mistakes.fix: Keep your chest angle fixed; if you need to swing, the weight is too heavy.
mistakes.why: Momentum moves the work from the back to the hips and loads the lower back with each jerk.

mistakes.name: Shoulders shrug
mistakes.looks: Shoulders ride up toward the ears at the top instead of squeezing back.
mistakes.fix: Pull your shoulder blades back and down, elbows toward your hips.
mistakes.why: Upper-trapezius dominance is the imbalance scapular training aims to avoid.

mistakes.name: Arms-only pull
mistakes.looks: The elbows bend but the shoulder blades never move; the bar stops short of the body.
mistakes.fix: Lead with your shoulder blades, then finish with the arms.
mistakes.why: Without scapular retraction the mid trapezius and rhomboids do little; seated rows give their highest activity when the blades move.

safety: Low-back pain: use a chest-supported or inverted row; the inverted row had the lowest spine load.
Shoulder pain: use a neutral grip and keep the elbows below shoulder height.
One-arm rows twist the trunk: start light if your back is sensitive.

variants.change: Palms up: elbows stay closer to the body, more biceps and lower lats.
Wide grip: elbows flare toward 60-75°, more rear delt and upper back.
Trunk near horizontal (about 80-90°), bar returns to the floor each rep.
One arm: free hand on a bench; the trunk must resist twisting, more oblique activity.
Palms facing: forearm 0, elbows close to the sides.
Pull line higher, toward the chest: elbows near 70-90° from the body, more rear delt and mid traps.
Band: load rises toward the end of the pull; control the return.

subtypes.name: Chest-supported row
subtypes.match: chest support|incline.*row|prone.*row|lying.*row|seal row|head supported|on rack|lying t bar|lying banded
subtypes.change: Chest on an incline bench or pad, legs and back passive; same arm and shoulder-blade path as the bent-over row.

subtypes.name: Inverted row
subtypes.match: inverted|suspen|suspended|ring.*row|towel row|bodyweight.*row|doorway|bed sheet|under table|between.*chairs|pulse row|parallel bars
subtypes.change: Hang under a bar or straps, body straight and face up, heels on the floor; pull the chest to the hands.

subtypes.name: Renegade row
subtypes.change: High plank on two dumbbells, feet wide; row one dumbbell while the hips stay square to the floor.

subtypes.name: Shoulder-blade squeeze
subtypes.change: Arms stay mostly still; only the shoulder blades pull back and glide forward. Small range, slow.

subtypes.name: Seated row
subtypes.match: seated|sitting|low row|high row|upper row|elevated row|standing.*row|kneeling|floor.*row|kayak|split stance|push pull|lever (alternating|narrow|one arm seated|row|seated|unilateral|low|one arm low|pronated|reverse grip high|reverse grip vertical|one arm lateral)
subtypes.change: Sitting tall with feet braced, trunk upright; arms reach forward and pull to the belly.
setup: Brace your feet on the plates with your knees slightly bent.
Hold the handle with straight arms, palms facing each other.
Sit tall with your chest up and shoulders down, leaning forward a little from the hips.

steps.text: Start with arms long and shoulder blades spread, back flat, leaning forward a little from the hips.
Squeeze your shoulder blades back first, then drive your elbows straight back, close to your sides.
Bring the handle to your belly with your chest tall, and hold for a moment.
Straighten your arms under control and let the shoulder blades glide forward again.

cues.cue: Tall, flat back. The trunk rocks only a little, it does not swing.
cues.why: A still, braced trunk keeps the work in the back muscles and the load on the lower back low.

cues.cue: Start each pull by squeezing your shoulder blades together.
cues.why: Rowing is one of the core exercises for the mid trapezius and rhomboids, which pull the shoulder blades back.

cues.cue: Elbows brush your sides and travel straight back.
cues.why: Thinking about the back, not the arms, raises lat activity and lowers rear-delt takeover.

cues.cue: Shoulders down, away from your ears.
cues.why: Shrugging shifts work to the upper trapezius instead of the mid and lower trapezius.

cues.cue: Arms fully long at the reach, handle to your belly at the squeeze.
cues.why: Letting the shoulder blades move through their range trains both the pull and the reach; fixing them only changes where the muscles work.

motion.basis: Shoulder-blade path (protraction at the reach, full retraction at the squeeze) from moseley1992, lehman2004 and padovan2025; upward rotation values estimated from humeral elevation using scapulohumeral rhythm data (ludewig2009). Trunk and hip angles for the bent-over row are coaching convention (nsca2016); fenwick2009 measured lumbar flexion only. Arm angles estimated.
